# AI Observability for Generative AI and LLM Models with Dynatrace

## Core Definition
"AI observability is the practice of collecting, analyzing, and correlating telemetry across your tech stack to understand how AI systems, agents, and LLMs behave in all environments including production."

## Key Metrics Monitored
- Stability: Success rates versus failure frequency
- Latency: Model response times
- Load: Request volume tracking
- Model drift: Accuracy changes from shifting data
- Data drift: Input data consistency monitoring
- Cost: Token usage and resource consumption

## Dynatrace Platform Capabilities
The platform provides continuous monitoring, logging, metrics analysis, domain-specific visualization, automated anomaly detection, and explainability features for AI systems.

## Integration Support
Dynatrace connects with OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, NVIDIA NIM, Ollama, LangChain, vector databases (Milvus, Weaviate, Qdrant), and infrastructure monitoring for GPU/TPU resources.

## Key Use Cases
Organizations use Dynatrace for service health tracking, quality and cost management, response quality evaluation through LLM-as-a-judge assessments, end-to-end tracing, and compliance auditing with complete data lineage.

## Agentic AI Capabilities
The platform monitors agent execution paths, tool invocations, and supports frameworks including OpenAI Agent SDK, LangGraph, CrewAI, and Google ADK.

## Evaluation Tools
The open-source dt-evals CLI runs continuous evaluations detecting user frustration, toxic responses, hallucinations, PII leakage, and prompt injection attempts.
